name: Beijing
summary: A capital in some form for over a thousand years, Beijing began as the frontier town of Ji and became the Mongol Dadu of Kublai Khan, described in wonder by Marco Polo. The Ming renamed it Beijing and built the Forbidden City and the Temple of Heaven; the Manchu Qing ruled a vast empire from it until 1912. From Tiananmen Gate, Mao proclaimed the People's Republic in 1949. Twice an Olympic host, it is today one of the largest and most powerful cities in the world.

figures.label: Capital since
figures.note: As Mongol Dadu; renamed Beijing in 1403.

figures.label: Setting

figures.label: Seat of

events.title: The town of Ji
events.body: A walled town called Ji, capital of the state of Yan, stands near modern Beijing.

events.title: A Liao capital
events.body: The Khitan Liao make the city one of their secondary capitals, Nanjing.

events.title: Jin Zhongdu
events.body: The Jurchen Jin make the city their central capital, Zhongdu.

events.title: Genghis Khan sacks it
events.body: Mongol armies destroy Zhongdu.

events.title: Kublai’s Dadu
events.body: Kublai Khan builds a grand new capital, Dadu, seat of the Yuan dynasty.

events.title: Marco Polo
events.body: The Venetian traveller describes the splendour of Kublai Khan’s capital.

events.title: The Ming take the city
events.body: The Ming overthrow the Mongols and rename the city Beiping.

events.title: Renamed Beijing
events.body: The Yongle Emperor makes it his capital and names it Beijing — “northern capital.”

events.title: The Forbidden City
events.body: Yongle completes the vast palace complex at the heart of the city.

events.title: The Temple of Heaven
events.body: The great ritual complex is built for the emperor’s sacrifices.

events.title: The outer wall
events.body: A new southern wall encloses the growing city.

events.title: The Qing conquest
events.body: The Manchu Qing seize Beijing as the Ming dynasty falls.

events.title: The Summer Palace
events.body: The Qing build lavish gardens and palaces northwest of the city.

events.title: The Old Summer Palace burned
events.body: British and French troops loot and burn the Yuanmingyuan during the Second Opium War.

events.title: The Boxer siege
events.body: The foreign legations are besieged in the Boxer Rebellion; an eight-nation army then sacks the city.

events.title: The last emperor abdicates
events.body: The Qing dynasty ends; the boy emperor Puyi abdicates in the Forbidden City.

events.title: The May Fourth Movement
events.body: Student protests in Beijing launch a new nationalist and cultural movement.

events.title: Japanese occupation
events.body: Japan seizes Beijing at the start of the wider war in China.

events.title: The People’s Republic
events.body: Mao Zedong proclaims the People’s Republic of China from Tiananmen Gate.

events.title: Remaking the centre
events.body: The old city walls come down and Tiananmen Square is vastly enlarged.

events.title: The Cultural Revolution
events.body: Mao launches the Cultural Revolution; Red Guards rally in Beijing.

events.title: Mao dies
events.body: Chairman Mao dies; his mausoleum is built on Tiananmen Square.

events.title: Tiananmen
events.body: Pro-democracy protests centred on Tiananmen Square are suppressed.

events.title: The Summer Olympics
events.body: Beijing hosts the Summer Games, announcing a rising China to the world.

events.title: The Winter Olympics
events.body: Beijing becomes the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Games.

places.name: The Forbidden City

places.name: Tiananmen Square
places.note: The great square before the palace, stage of modern China.

places.name: Temple of Heaven
places.note: The ritual complex where emperors prayed for good harvests.

places.name: The Summer Palace

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.

dynasties.note: Dynasties and houses that shaped Beijing.

list.name: The Yuan (Mongol) dynasty
list.legacy: Dadu, the first imperial capital here
list.summary: Kublai Khan built Dadu as the capital of a Mongol empire that spanned Asia.

list.name: The Ming dynasty
list.legacy: The Forbidden City and Temple of Heaven
list.summary: The Ming made Beijing the capital and built its greatest monuments.

list.name: The Qing dynasty
list.legacy: A vast empire ruled from the Forbidden City
list.summary: China’s last dynasty ruled a vast empire from Beijing until 1912.
